chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn Ahmad, from one of his companions, from Suleiman ibn ibn Ja'far al-Ja'fari, from his father, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
Rasool-Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'Allah, Blessed and Exalted, made the prayer obligatory five times and appointed for the deceased, from each prayer, one Takbeer.'
ai.seo_question: Why are there five Takbeers in the funeral prayer?
ai.summary: This hadith from Al-Kafi establishes the divine origin of the five Takbeers in Salat al-Mayyit by linking them to the five daily obligatory prayers, a view supported by Shia jurists who see this as a specific legislative decree (hukm) rather than merely a symbolic gesture. It highlights the continuity between the believer's daily worship and the final rite of passage, emphasizing that the funeral prayer is an extension of the individual's personal Salah. This narration is foundational in Shia fiqh for determining the number of Takbeers, distinguishing it from other schools that may vary in number or emphasis.
